source.title: Efficiency vs. Alignment: Investigating Safety and Fairness Risks in Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of LLMs
source.authors: M. Taraghi; Y. Pequignot; Amin Nikanjam; Mohamed Amine Merzouk; F. Khomh

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign fine-tuning changes harmful-prompt safety, using PEFT methods and a safety-score benchmark rather than the original study's fine-tuning recipe.
record.gate_note: The paper tests benign PEFT and harmful-request safety outcomes, so it bears on V2. It does not test harmful-example fine-tuning, token-position KL, opening-token prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, or safety localization in parameters. Its discussion of safety neurons is an explanation attributed to prior work, not a result of this study. Fairness results are outside the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes safety-trained instruct models on benign data (UltraFeedback, UltraChat, CodeAlpaca) with four PEFT methods. It measures harmful-request compliance on HEx-PHI, the original paper's benchmark, as change from each base model. This bears directly on V2. The method differs from the original: PEFT rather than full fine-tuning, and a LLaMA-Guard 2 judge. It tests nothing about V1 or V3–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the aggregate safety change is non-significant, with no consistent direction. Adapters yield significant safety gains, while prompt-based methods yield significant losses. Gemma shows the only significant base-model decline and LLaMA is largely unaffected. CodeAlpaca lowers safety vs base but does not differ significantly from matched conversational runs.
record.recipe_differences: Uses benign PEFT (LoRA, IA3, Prompt-Tuning, and P-Tuning) on instruction-tuned models, with HEx-PHI safety scoring; it does not reproduce the original harmful-example fine-tuning intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by PEFT family and base model. LoRA rank, prompt virtual-token count, and IA3 target-module placement change the magnitude of results; the paper reports no stable rank or target-module difference in its paired tests. Dataset, epoch count, and learning rate show limited or inconsistent safety effects. Judge choice changes some unsafe-response rates but preserves the broad method ordering.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign PEFT degrades BBQ-Lite fairness accuracy and raises bias magnitude, mostly under prompt-based methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning erodes fairness/bias behaviour as well as safety.

fits_no_version.finding: Safety change correlates positively with utility and fairness-accuracy change (Spearman, Fig. 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety erosion under benign fine-tuning co-occurs with general capability loss.

record.problems: Safety is measured using automated judges rather than full human annotation; the main analysis uses one safety judge, with an alternative-judge check on a limited slice. The experiment covers four 7–8B instruction-tuned model families and selected datasets/settings. Ten models with inference failures and 19 utility outliers were excluded. Many per-setting result values are presented in figures or appendices rather than stated in the main text.
record.rows_left_out: Did not create separate rows for every one of the 235 analyzed variants, every model-by-method interaction, or all category-by-method profiles summarized in Figures 2–5 and the appendix tables; the paper does not state all corresponding numeric values in the text. The selected rows retain the aggregate, model, category, sensitivity, coding-extension, and judge-comparison results needed for V2.

untested.parts: Full-parameter fine-tuning; models outside 7–8B; benign data chosen to sit close to harmful data, or identity-shifting data as in Qi et al.; datasets other than UltraFeedback/UltraChat/CodeAlpaca; full-size training sets (only 10–34% subsamples were used).
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
No localization of safety in weights; the safety-neuron explanation is cited from prior work.

missing.what: Per-method and per-model significance vs base for overall safety: IA3, LoRA, Prompt-Tuning and P-Tuning vs base are all significant; only Gemma is significant among models
Base-model HEx-PHI safety scores per category (LLaMA 93.94, Gemma 92.12, Qwen 83.94, Mistral 55.15), needed to read changes as compliance rates
Effect of training choices: SFT vs DPO, UltraChat vs UltraFeedback, 1 vs 5 epochs, LR 2e-5 vs 1e-3 show no consistent safety effect; DPO SD 3.45 vs SFT 9.85
CodeAlpaca category-level safety declines vs base, significant in nine categories; no significant safety difference vs matched UltraFeedback runs

record.verdict_notes: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 lacks safety alignment, so its rows bear weakly on V2. The Table IX sensitivity rows have no per-setting significance test vs base. The Table XII LLaMA-Guard rows duplicate Table IX, and the GPT-4.1 rows have no base-model rate. This is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful examples were used for fine-tuning.
Tests benign PEFT on selected instruction-tuned models and datasets; does not test the full range of ordinary or carefully selected benign datasets, or full-parameter fine-tuning.
No per-token KL divergence or response-position analysis.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.
PEFT methods and some rank settings are tested, but the study does not test whether a localized set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Does not test whether training data or objectives produce token-depth shallowness.
Does not train or test a method intended to spread safety beyond the first response tokens.

relationships.condition: Prompt-based PEFT (Prompt-Tuning, P-Tuning); Gemma-7B-it; CodeAlpaca coding extension
relationships.reason: Prompt-based methods lower HEx-PHI safety significantly vs base (−6 to −15 pts in Table IX). Gemma degrades significantly in all categories. Benign coding PEFT lowers safety significantly: r4, r5, r8, r18–r21, r26.
relationships.display_finding: Prompt-based methods lowered HEx-PHI safety by 6 to 15 points versus the base model, Gemma-7B-it degraded in all categories, and benign coding PEFT also lowered safety significantly.
